questions.question: Ileana Citaristi is the first classical dancer of foreign origin who was conferred the Padma Shri Award in 2006 for her contributions to ______.
questions.solution:

__**Ileana Citaristi **__

 
• Ileana Citaristi is an **Odissi and Chhau dancer** and dance teacher from **Italy **who currently resides in Bhubaneswar, India.
 
• Citaristi founded her own **dance school in 1994 **after studying Odissi under **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra.** 
 
• She is a master of the** Mayurbhanj Chhau**, which she studied under the guidance of **Guru Hari Nayak.** 
 
• She has received the **designation of acharya of Chhau from the Sangeet Mahavidyalya of Bhubaneswar.**
 
• She won the **Best Choreography prize **at the 43rd National Film Awards in 1995 for Yugant.

• In 2006, she became the first dancer of foreign origin to be conferred the Padma Shri for her contributions to Odissi.

questions.question: The term ‘Follow – On’ is used in which of the following games/sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** ‘Follow – On’ **is used in** cricket.**
 
• A team who **batted second in **the sport of cricket but scored significantly **fewer runs** than the team that** bat first** can be obliged to** follow-on,** or to play their **second innings **right after their first.
 
• The **side that batted first** may impose the follow-on.
 
• By** speeding up the second innings** of the second team, it aims to lower the** likelihood of a drawn outcome.**
 
• Only in the** types of cricket **where each team often bats twice—most notably **domestic first-class cricket** and** international Test cricket—**does the follow-on occur.
 
• **Boundary, LBW, Beamer, Appeal, Bails, Dolly, Edge** etc. are other terms used in cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hockey:**

 
 
• **16-yard hit, Advancing, Back-line, Bully, Center pass , Clearing, Dangerous Play,** etc. are some of the terms used in the game of **hockey**. 
 
 
 
• **Badminton:**
 
 
• **The backcourt, Birdie, Carry, Center position, Cross-court, Drop shot, Flick, Forecourt**, etc. are some of the terms used in the game of **badminton**.
 
 
 
• **Football:**
 
 
• **Line of scrimmage, fumble, muff, huddle, blitz, sack, scramble, special teams, **etc. are some of the terms used in the game football.

questions.question: Which ecosystem is the only one that does NOT thrive on solar energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems exist at depths exceeding 1,000 meters on the ocean floor.**
 
• These ecosystems feature **hydrothermal vents, fissures in the Earth's crust, emitting hot, mineral-rich fluids **into the surrounding seawater.
 
• Vents are formed by **tectonic and volcanic processes**, releasing heated water containing high mineral concentrations.
 
• Life in these extreme environments includes bacteria, archaea, and specialized organisms **adapted to high pressure, darkness, and temperature fluctuations.**
 
• Unique microbial communities thrive around vents, utilizing **chemosynthesis **to produce organic matter from inorganic compounds.
 
• Hydrothermal vent ecosystems support diverse life forms such as **tube worms, clams, shrimp, and octopuses.**
 
• They contribute to global **biogeochemical **cycles and offer insights into the origins of life on Earth and potential extraterrestrial habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **ecosystem is the basic ecological unit **in which living organisms interact among themselves and with their surrounding physical environment.
 
• **Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem**, the sun (sunlight) is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on earth.
 
• Out of the total incident solar radiation, **only 50% of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR).**
 
• **Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR **and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world.

questions.question: Which Gharana was propounded by Bade Fateh Ali Khan and Ali Baksh Jarnail Khan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Patiala Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Patiala Gharana is one of the vocal Gharanas of Hindustani classical music, named after the city of **Patiala **in Punjab.
 
• Patiala Gharana was originally founded by **Mian Kallu**, it is widely acknowledged that it was** Ali Baksh Khan** and **Fateh Ali Khan** who popularised the Patiala tradition of singing.
 
• Singers in the Gharana are known for their emotionally evocative and sensual singing style, and particular emphasis is placed on clear diction and enunciation.
 
• The Patiala Gharana was inspired by and influenced by four musical Gharanas — **Delhi**, **Gwalior**, **Riva**, and **Jaipur**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior Gharana**:

 
 
• It is considered the oldest Khayal Gharana in Indian classical music.
 
• Nanthan khan was the founder of this Gharana
 
• It was founded in the first half of the 19th century and became popular during the Mughal ruler Akbar period.
 
• Mian Tansen was one of the first and most famous vocalists who came from Gwalior.
 
 
 
• **Agra Gharana**:
 
 
• Hajisujan Khan was the founder of Agra Gharana.
 
• Agra Gharana is a blend of Khayal Gayaki and Dhrupad-Dhamar.
 
 
 
• **Bhendi Bazaar Gharana**:
 
 
• It was founded around 1890 by brothers Chhajju Khan, Nazir Khan, and Khadim Hussain Khan in the Bhendi bazaar area of Mumbai

questions.question: In how many categories are loans provided under the MUDRA loan scheme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__4__**

__
 
• **4 categories** are provided under the MUDRA loan scheme.
 
• The categories are **Shishu, Kishore, Tarun, and Tarun +**.
 
• **Shishu** category covers loans up to ₹50,000, **Kishore** category covers loans above ₹50,000 and up to ₹5 lakh, and **Tarun** category covers loans above ₹5 lakh and up to ₹10 lakh. **Tarun Plus**: Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakhs

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The MUDRA loan scheme was launched by the Government of India in **April 2015**.
 
• MUDRA stands for **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency**.
 
• The scheme is part of the **Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY)**.
 
• It aims to provide financial support to the non-corporate, non-farm small/micro enterprises.
 
• The loans under the MUDRA scheme are collateral-free and can be availed from **commercial banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs, and NBFCs**.
 
• The scheme has been instrumental in fostering entrepreneurship and generating employment in the country.

questions.question: Which of the following were **NOT **a part of a citadel in Harrapan architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Residential buildings for masses.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The most interesting urban feature of the Harappan civilization is its town planning.**

 
• The citadel contains** large structures **which might have functioned as administrative or ritual centres.
 
• In some cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, special buildings were constructed on the citadel.
 
 
• For example, in Mohenjodaro, a very special tank, which archaeologists call the Great Bath, was built in the citadel area.
 
• Perhaps important people took a dip in this tank on special occasions.
 
• Other cities, such as Kalibangan and Lothal had fire altars, where sacrifices may have been performed.
 
• And some cities like Mohenjodaro, Harappa, and Lothal had elaborate storehouses.
 
 
 
• The **residential buildings are built in the lower town. Hence they are not part of the citadel.**
 
• The streets intersect each other at right angles in a criss-cross pattern.
 
• It divides the city into several **residential blocks**. The main street is connected by narrow lanes.
 
• The doors of the houses opened in these lanes and not the main streets.
 
• The houses of common people, however, differed in size from **single-room houses in Harappa to bigger structures**. The houses were largely built of **burnt bricks.**

• **Megasthenes** was the envoy sent by Seleucus I to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• After Alexander's death, Seleucus established control over a vast territory that included parts of the Middle East and Asia.
 
• The alliance and diplomatic relationship between Seleucus and Chandragupta Maurya were significant in shaping the geopolitical landscape of the time.
 
• The **Indica** by Megasthenes, though lost in its original form, survives through quotations by later authors such as Strabo and Arrian.

• **Mayurasharma **a Kannada scholar and a native of Talagunda was the founder of the Kadamba Kingdom of Banavasi.
 
• Banavasi is said to be the oldest town in Karnataka earlier known as Konkanapura.

questions.question: Which physicist is known to establish the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**James Prescott Joule**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **James Prescott Joule** is renowned for establishing the relationship between mechanical work and heat transfer.
 
• Joule's experiments demonstrated that** heat and mechanical work are interchangeable, leading to the formulation of the first law of thermodynamics**.
 
• His work laid the foundation for** the principle of conservation of energy, **which states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another.
 
• The unit of energy, **the joule (J), **is named in his honor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Henry** is known for Henry's law, which relates the solubility of gases in liquids to pressure.
 
• **Hermann Helmholtz** made significant contributions to the fields of physiology and physics, particularly in the study of energy conservation and electrodynamics.
 
• **John Dalton** is famous for his pioneering work in the development of modern atomic theory and his research on color blindness.
 
• Joule's work was pivotal in advancing the Industrial Revolution, providing a scientific basis for the efficient use of energy in engines and other machinery.

questions.question: Which of the following lakes is correctly paired with the state in which it is located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhimtal lake – Uttarakhand.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Bhimtal Lake:**__

__
 
• Bhimtal Lake is a lake in the town of Bhimtal, in the Indian state of Uttarakhand, with a masonry dam built in 1883 creating the storage facility
 
• It is the **largest lake in the Kumaon region**, known as the **"lake district of India”**.
 
• The lake provides a drinking water supply and supports aquaculture with a variety of fish species.
 
• There is an **island at the centre of the lake **which has been developed as a **tourist attraction** and has an aquarium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**__**Dal Lake:**__

__
 
• Dal is a lake in** Srinagar** and is the** second largest** in the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is named the “**Jewel in the crown of Kashmir” or “Srinagar’s Jewel”.**
 
• The lake is part of a **natural wetland,** including its floating gardens. The floating gardens, known as “Rad” in Kashmiri, blossom with lotus flowers during July and August.
 
• The lake is located in the Zabarwan mountain valley, in the foothills of the Shankracharya hills, which surrounds it on three sides.

**Chilika Lake:**__

__
 
• Chilika lake is the** largest brackish water lagoon **situated in **Odisha.**
 
• It is the **largest coastal lagoon** in India and the second-largest brackish lagoon in the world after the New Caledonian Barrier Reef.
 
• It has been listed as a **UNESCO World Heritage site.**
 
• It is the highest lake in India and is the** largest wintering ground for migratory birds **in the subcontinent of India.

**Loktak Lake:**__

 
• Loktak Lake situated in** Manipur** is the** largest freshwater lake in North East India** and is famous for the **phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil and organic matter at various stages of decomposition) floating over it.
 
• The lake is located at **Moirang** in Manipur state, India.
 
• **Loktak Day** is observed every year on the **15th of October **at the periphery of the Loktak lake.

questions.question: Who won the bronze medal in womens boxing in Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Event:**

 
 
• Women's Welterweight Boxing (64-69 kg)
 
 
 
• **Medal:**
 
 
• Bronze Medal
 
• **Lovlina Borgohain** secured the bronze after reaching the semi-finals. As per **Olympic boxing rules**, both losing semi-finalists are awarded bronze medals.
 
 
 
• **Journey to the Medal:**
 
 
• Lovlina won her quarter-final match against Nien-Chin Chen of Chinese Taipei with a convincing 4-1 victory, ensuring her a place in the semi-finals and a guaranteed medal.
 
• In the semi-finals, she faced the top-seeded Turkish boxer** Busenaz Sürmeneli**, a tough opponent, and despite her efforts, she lost the bout 0-5, securing the bronze

• **MC Mary Kom:**
 
 
• A legendary boxer with six World Championships and a bronze medal at the 2012 London Olympics.
 
• Known as the "Magnificent Mary," she is a pioneering figure in Indian women’s boxing.
 
 
 
• **Aditi Ashok:**
 
 
• A professional golfer who finished 4th at the Tokyo Olympics 2020, narrowly missing a medal.

questions.question: TH Vinayakram, a famous musician, is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghatam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Ghatam**

 
 
• A Ghatam is a large, narrow-mouthed earthenware pot used as a percussion instrument.
 
• The ghatam is a percussion instrument that is utilized in several Indian repertoires.
 
• The ghatam is an Indian percussion instrument that dates back thousands of years. It's a narrow-mouthed clay pot.
 
• A small amount of plasticine clay or water can be used to change the pitch significantly.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16ce91c8903f77f0a7d3059a0eca574979fc2791ef6b6e736d431834b45de744.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mridangam**​​​

 
 
• The mridangam is a percussion instrument of ancient origin.
 
• One of the most ancient drums of India, the mridangam, which literally means 'body of clay,' originated in South India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/556141b52bec994d00221c0f7b5a15369ea88dd74f0d4759954a0588928a955f.png] 

 
• **Sarod**

 
 
• Sarod is a **stringed instrument** made of coconut shell, tun wood, drone, shikri, and ivory.
 
• This is a traditional instrument that is found in various parts of** North India**.
 
• A popular plucked instrument, it is used in North Indian classical music for **solo concerts**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9589ac1f9c24254958172280384c4a47a3759de04a84019ecc19f60dc6d023be.png] 

 
• Tabla

 
 
• Tabla is a small drum or Pair of Drums tuned to different pitches playing with hands.
 
• It was invented by Amir khusru __in 1738.
 
• The right side is called the Tabla and the left, the Bayan or Dagga.
 
• It is a type of Avanaddha vadya or Membranophone.
